reviewMethod: Read every stored occurrence as a complete encounter, address, verse, title, or narrative unit rather than trusting the container title alone.
Treated MasterName only as the utterer of the exact headword; acting, quoted, discussed, and section masters belong in ContextMasters.
Independently reran zc.verify on all 113 KWICs and required both returned FromLb and ToLb to equal the stored span.
Compared the current entry bytes to the exact SHA-256 values below; no entry was edited during review.

reasons: Occurrence 3 is not safely anonymous: it is in 天隱修禪師語錄, and the same headword-bearing address is preserved under Tianyin Yuanxiu in J/J25/J25nB171.xml. The title and parallel-witness rungs therefore resolve the authored voice as Tianyin Yuanxiu.
Occurrence 2 correctly assigns the headword to the unnamed monk, but omits the named responding record-owner from ContextMasters.
The explanation says the response is ‘intended to help them,’ importing intent in vocabulary expressly barred by rule #0; describe the attested public function without asserting intention.

Keeping MasterName null for narrated bodily actions is correct, but occurrences 5 and 6 leave ContextMasters empty even though the complete teaching-seat units contain a particular master performing the action.
Rule 10 requires every master to be named: resolve the acting masters and record them as person-described or case-figure while preserving narrated/impersonal MasterName null.
Later named raisers are distinguished from the one editorial heading, and Yunyan/Daowu remain correctly identified as case figures.
Occurrence 3 says 問：樹凋葉落時如何？師云：體露金風. The unnamed monk utters the question but not the headword; the resident master utters the exact headword after 師云.
Its current reviewed-unnamed monastic-questioner attribution and GrammarEvidence invert the two turns and must be corrected after resolving the resident master from the complete section.
Direct speech and embedded named quotations are assigned to their actual utterers across the seven complete cases.
Questioner, named utterer, and narrator-governed placement are correctly separated.
Each headword occurrence belongs to the named address, verse, or later raising voice recorded in MasterName.
Shennong is the invoked figure while the four named masters remain the actual authored or spoken voices.
Five master utterances and the named disciples’ request are correctly distinguished; the respondent is not substituted for the disciples.
The elder’s 何不領話 is not misassigned to Muzhou, and the remaining named turns are correctly attributed.
Contents and rules prose remain narrator-governed; only Chaoding Yuxuan’s spoken instruction carries his MasterName.
Direct master speech, the embedded Buddha quotation, and the two unnamed monks’ questions are separated by exact turn.
Zhaozhou’s spoken instruction is distinguished from six narrator-governed striking actions.
All four exact phrases belong to the named commenting masters, with Huangbo retained as the invoked case figure rather than the utterer.
The Zhaozhou question, named discourses, biographical narration, and final unnamed monk’s question are correctly classified.
The named non-master commentator is not forced into MasterName, and the five master utterers are correctly named.
The two embedded Buddha turns and the two later master deployments are attributed to their exact voices.
The lay official’s question remains non-master speech, while five later master raisings are named correctly.
Five named utterers and the genuinely source-anonymous feast-day address are distinguished without assigning the following section’s master backward.
Three named authored voices and the unnamed monk’s clearly marked 僧曰 turn are correctly separated.
